title: Evaluating the Feasibility of an Artificial-Intelligence Based Clinical Decision Support Tool for People With Chronic Lung Disease
official: Building Equitable and Feasible Clinical Decision Support Tools for Population Health Management of People Living With Chronic Lung Disease
summary:
Patients living with chronic lung diseases (CLD) are at high risk of frailty, malnutrition, and depression. However, many of the interventions targeting these conditions are underutilized. Thus, artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support systems (AI-CDSS) offer a promising approach to guide targeted interventions for this population and reduce risk of hospitalization.

The purpose of this study is to assess the acceptability and feasibility of a new AI-CDSS for community-dwelling patients with CLD. The goal of this AI-CDSS is to predict the probability that patients would benefit from 5 frailty- and depression-focused interventions (pulmonary rehabilitation, physical therapy, fall-risk assessment, nutrition consultation, and depression consultation).

In this study, pulmonologists will review the AI-CDSS's predictions and have the option to recommend referrals for their patients. If a referral is recommended, the study team will contact the patient to discuss the referral and start the referral process. All participants will then complete a semi-structured interview and feedback survey asking their opinions about the AI-CDSS and the study referral process.

interventions.name: Artificial intelligence-based clinical decision support tool for recommending referrals for chronic lung disease patients

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Pulmonologists:

1. Cares for patients with chronic lung disease at Penn Medicine
2. Volunteered to participate in the pilot study prior to study recruitment

Patients:

1. Had two diagnostic codes consistent with a chronic lung disease (J44, J43, J41, J42, J84, J99)
2. Had at least one outpatient visit with a participating Penn Medicine pulmonologist
3. Had at least one hospitalization or ED visit for an exacerbation of a CLD
4. Has at least one AI-generated referral suggestion reviewed and approved by: (a) the study pulmonologist and (b) their outpatient Penn Medicine pulmonologist

Caregivers:

1. Asked to be included in the study by the patient
2. Able to complete the consent, referral discussion, interview and survey together with the patient

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Patients who received a lung transplant
2. Patients actively listed for lung transplant
3. Patients actively admitted to the hospital
4. Patients who have a "Research Do Not Contact" status
5. All individuals who are non-English speaking
6. All individuals under the age of 18 years old
7. All individuals unable to provide informed consent in the opinion of the investigator
